## What it finds

A key written straight into an MCP server entry: in its `env`, its headers, its arguments, its
command or its URL. Files such as `.mcp.json` and `.cursor/mcp.json` are often committed, and
README snippets say "paste your token here".

The print names the server and the field, and shows the key masked, for example `sk_l…(len 36)`.

## Why it matters

MCP configs are among the most copied agent files. A key in one is as exposed as a key in any
settings file, so this is a critical print.

## How to fix

1. Rotate the key. Revoke it and create a new one.
2. Make the MCP server read the key from an environment variable instead of the config file.
   The fix in each print says how, for that agent.

## Limits

- Pattern-based only. An odd key format can be missed.
- AP005 replaces [AP002](/agentprint/checks/ap002/) for the same key in the same file. Keys
  elsewhere in that file stay AP002.
- agentprint never starts or contacts an MCP server.
